_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the equaliser's band layout, presets and limits.
Both front ends read these numbers rather than each keeping a copy:
* Python  — eqcore/spec.py loads this file at import time.
* Browser — web/spec.js is GENERATED from this file by tools/gen_web_spec.py.
Edit this file, then run `python tools/gen_web_spec.py`. CI fails if the
A band declares its Q either directly ('q', used for the shelves) or as a
bandwidth in octaves ('bandwidth_octaves', used for the bells), from which
Q = sqrt(2^N) / (2^N - 1). Deriving it is what makes the bells tile the
spectrum evenly instead of leaving holes between them.

presets.name: Flat / Reset
presets.note: All bands at 0 dB — the filter chain becomes a pass-through.

presets.name: Bass Boost
presets.note: Low-shelf lift under 60 Hz plus a bell at 122 Hz for weight and punch.

presets.name: Vocal Boost
presets.note: Cuts rumble, lifts 1–5 kHz where speech intelligibility lives.

presets.name: Treble Boost
presets.note: High-shelf air above 8 kHz with a presence lift for detail.

presets.name: Loudness (V-shape)
presets.note: Boosts both extremes and scoops the mids — the classic smiley curve.

presets.name: Podcast / Speech
presets.note: Steep low-end cut to kill room rumble, forward upper mids.
